### Subtle 105–110% punch-in on key phrases
<a id="fx-subtle-punch-in"></a>

Subtle 105–110% punch-ins on key phrases and when each numbered section starts (L06); Rahul punches in on emphasis.

**How:** CapCut: split at the phrase, Scale 105–110 on the segment (or keyframe an eased zoom); ffmpeg: crop=iw/1.08:ih/1.08,scale=1080:1920.

> Subtle 105–110% punch-ins on key phrases

### Khandala pans and push-ins were linear
<a id="fx-khandala-linear-moves"></a>

Khandala animates its photos with slow pans and push-ins (sun to subject, cliff + cactus), but our ffmpeg build moved them at constant speed (linear), the opposite of L03's rule.

**How:** ffmpeg: zoompan with an eased z expression; CapCut: keyframe scale/position with Graphs ease.

`edit` · formats: reel30, yt-short · niches: travel · our-take · from [KH](../sources/KH.md), [L03](../sources/L03.md) · ⚠ [C2](../clashes.md#c2)

### B&W freeze for sarcastic punchlines
<a id="fx-bw-freeze-punchline"></a>

Desaturate and hold the frame on a sarcastic line.

**How:** CapCut: Freeze frame + Adjust saturation −100; ffmpeg: hue=s=0 on a tpad/loop hold.

### Demo each effect on your own shot
<a id="l10-apply-effect-on-yourself"></a>

Each technique is applied to his own footage as he names it: grade-panel sliders move and his saturation measurably drops (SATAVG ~8 to ~4.5 at 56 s), his shot shrinks into the centre of the 3x3 wall, the words go behind his head. It works as proof and as a pattern interrupt.

**How:** In the storyboard, mark the word where each effect should switch on in your own shot, not just on the example.

### Before/after slider reveals the grade
<a id="l10-grade-slider-reveal"></a>

The source shows a warm look switched on, then a vertical slider wipes across to take it off: a before/after reveal. Chandler: FFmpeg makes the colour change, Remotion the slider.

**How:** Stack graded over ungraded and animate a vertical wipe mask with an eased move. CapCut: overlay the graded copy and keyframe a linear mask.

> FFMpeg for the color change and Remotion again for the slider effect.

## Graphics

### Entrances ease out, exits ease in
<a id="fx-ease-out-entrances"></a>

Things that arrive ease out (fast, then a long brake, "as if set down by a steady hand"); things that leave ease in (slow start, then away). Oren's overlays slide in with spring/ease-out.

**How:** CapCut: keyframe → Graphs → ease presets; VN: keyframe curve; ffmpeg: 1-pow(1-t/d,3) in, pow(t/d,3) out instead of t/d.

> For everything that comes in: ease out.

`graphics` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long · niches: all · stated · from [L03](../sources/L03.md), [L06](../sources/L06.md), [L07](../sources/L07.md) · ⚠ [C2](../clashes.md#c2)

### UI and text pops: spring with slight overshoot
<a id="fx-spring-ui"></a>

Interface elements and text pops use a spring that overshoots its target a little, then settles (spring/bounce slide-ins in L02; spring UI cards in L07).

**How:** CapCut: Animation → In → Bounce/Spring-style; HyperFrames/CSS: cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1).

> It overshoots its target just a little, then settles back.

### Text behind your head
<a id="l10-text-behind-head"></a>

Cut the speaker out with a person-segmentation model and put words on a layer between the background and the person, so the title sits behind the head. He uses it for the topic title, his brand name ("Chandler Intelligence", two-tone) and the CTA keyword "EDIT" (huge, outlined, low opacity).

**How:** AI: "cut me out with a person segmentation model, put the words behind me" (he renders with Remotion; HyperFrames can do the same). CapCut: duplicate the clip, Remove background on the top copy, put the text track between the two copies.

> Tell Claude to cut you out with a person's segmentation model, then put the words behind you using Remotion.

`graphics` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: all · stated · from [L10](../sources/L10.md)

### 3x3 wall of reels proves a trend
<a id="l10-3x3-reel-wall"></a>

To show that "lots of people are doing this", his shot shrinks into the centre tile of a 3x3 grid and 8 downloaded reels pop in around it, one per frame. The grid then stays on as the thumbnail.

**How:** Download 8 examples with yt-dlp; prompt: "Shrink my shot into the centre tile of a 3x3 grid, then pop 8 of these reels in around it, one per frame."

> Shrink my shot into the centre tile of a 3x3 grid, then pop 8 of these reels in around it, one per frame.

### View-count pill on every example
<a id="l11-view-count-proof-pill"></a>

A dark rounded pill with an eye icon and the example's views (40.5M, 339K, 4.9M, 4.7M, 1.9M, 3.6M, 28M) sits lower-centre on every borrowed clip, so each claim arrives with proof. The numbers are the creator's overlay, not verified.

**How:** When citing any result (your old reel, a benchmark, a lift), show the number in a small dark pill with an icon; HyperFrames card or a CapCut text box with rounded background.
